task: Restaurant rival progression: Round 1 loss/draw offers REMATCH (Waiter 1 again, no solo phase, no cinematic) or FINISH (final question); a Round 1 win brings a visibly different Waiter 2 with the FULL existing rival introduction, then a harder Round 2 that always ends in the final question. Reuse the existing entrance, challenge modal, score, result stage, speech and customer/belt systems; do not redesign them.
notes: Read DESIGN_DECISIONS.md (Restaurant entries 2026-09-14..19) and SPEC.md section 4 first. Record this pass as a DESIGN_DECISIONS entry dated 2026-09-19 (what, why, rejected alternatives listed at the end of these notes) and revise the SPEC paragraphs it supersedes (result moment → final question, turnaround partner, rival levels).
Scope: only Normal (2) and Challenge (3), the levels with RIVAL_LEVELS enabled. Easy is unchanged. A shift that ends before the rush (no rival arrived) is unchanged.

PURE PROGRESSION MODEL: add src/minigames/restaurant/rivalProgression.js + rivalProgression.test.mjs. It owns no scene/DOM. Suggested API: createRivalProgression() with state { round: 1|2, rivalId: 'waiter1'|'waiter2', attempt (1-based count of Round 1 battles), phase }, and resolveRound(outcome) → one of { next: 'choice' } (round 1, outcome 'rival' or 'draw'), { next: 'round2-intro' } (round 1, outcome 'player'), { next: 'final-question' } (round 2, any outcome). chooseRematch() → { next: 'round1-rematch' } (valid only while awaiting the choice; increments attempt), chooseFinish() → { next: 'final-question' }. startRound2() valid only after a round-1 win. Anything else returns null and changes nothing. There is no round 3: after round 2 resolves, every further call returns null. Export ROUND_TWO tuning constants from here or rival.js/conveyor.js (see TUNING).

ROUND LENGTH: a rematch and Round 2 are competitive from their first customer. Their customer count is the competitive part of the Round 1 shift: DIFFICULTY[level].total − RUSH_PLAYER_DELIVERIES (Normal 6, Challenge 10). Derive it from those two constants (the controller's browser harness shortens DIFFICULTY.total by patching the served index.js text 'count: 4, total: 9,' — keep that literal shape). Round-end detection (updateRoundEnd) must work per round: compare this round's resolved customers to this round's count, not the cumulative shift total.

OUTCOME: every round's result must still come from competitionOutcome(...) exported by rushTrigger.js with the same signature (the controller's harness patches that function to force outcomes). Score per round via createCompetitionScore baseline as today: each new round (rematch or Round 2) starts at きみ 0 ・ ウェイター 0 and the pill shows 0–0 as soon as the round begins.

RESULT STAGE BRANCH (index.js beginResultStage/updateResultStage/beginResultQuestion): the reaction (3.6 s) and settling run exactly as now for every round. At the point where the rival currently asks 'What food do you like?': (a) Round 1 rival win or draw → the rival's speech bubble shows STRINGS.rivalRematchAsk and the challenge reply UI (same panel, same buttons component, same focus/arrow/Enter/Space/click handling, same modal class, Talk forced hidden/disabled, bubbles hidden) offers exactly two choices STRINGS.rematchChoices[0] (rematch) and [1] (finish). No typewriter needed for this short line (use it only if it is free). (b) FINISH → existing beginResultQuestion unchanged (Waiter 1 asks LESSON.question, promptAnswer, completion). (c) Round 1 player win → no choice, no question; go to the ROUND 2 TRANSITION. (d) Round 2 any outcome → existing beginResultQuestion with Waiter 2 as the partner. Nothing else may reach the final question early, and the final question must never be skipped: losing never blocks completion.

REMATCH TRANSITION: hide the choice panel, fade/cut back to the gameplay room camera (reuse the existing camera presets; a short black transition or camera ease is fine), run RESET BETWEEN ROUNDS, put Waiter 1 back at its gameplay start (it is already 'arrived', no entrance walk, no jingle, no close-up, no title), put the player at the normal start, show STRINGS.rematchCue via showPhaseCue (like ランチラッシュ！), then start the competitive round immediately: conveyor in Round 1 rush mode (conveyor.startRush() or equivalent at Round 1 rush values), director in rush with owner-aware budget, rival AI active with the SAME RIVAL_LEVELS[level] config as the first battle. No rushTrigger / solo phase / 1.6 s beat.

ROUND 2 TRANSITION: after the Round 1 result settles (player win), fade back to the room camera; Waiter 1 leaves (walks out the front-left aisle it came in by and is then hidden, or is hidden during the fade — prefer the short walk if it is clean; it must not stay in the room or keep any AI/claims), RESET BETWEEN ROUNDS, and then play Waiter 2's FULL introduction through the existing rivalChallenge path: a fresh createRivalChallenge instance, room frozen (paused), the same BA-BAM jingle, entrance walk up the same aisle, camera follow, 0.2 s turn, 2.0 s close-up with the challenger pose, title reveal (STRINGS.rival2Title), 0.8 s camera return, floating ウェイター label + panel, furigana-safe typewriter with STRINGS.rival2Challenge, then all three STRINGS.rival2ChallengeReplies at once. Any reply → the existing 0.55 s nod → Round 2 starts immediately (no solo phase). Every timing, key handling rule and HUD/modal rule of Waiter 1's intro applies unchanged (Space/Enter/tap reveals the typing and that press cannot answer; Talk hidden and disabled while the modal is active). Generalise the existing functions (beginRivalChallenge, updateRushSequence, showChallengePanel, renderChallengeTypewriter, applyChallengerPoseAfterAnimation, updateRivalEntranceLabel, rivalTitle text) to act on the CURRENT rival character and CURRENT line/replies/title; do not duplicate a second cinematic system.

WAITER 2 CHARACTER: build it in buildWorld next to Waiter 1 (hidden until its intro) with characters.create using a DIFFERENT Kenney model: not 'r' (Waiter 1), not characters.playerModel, not any of CUSTOMER_MODELS ['e','f','i','m','q'] — pick one whose hair and face read clearly different from 'r' at the room camera. Different tint and a clearly different uniform: a dark apron (e.g. black or deep red, emissive enough to read on the dark floor) instead of Waiter 1's white one, plus one small procedural accessory built with addPart from the same box geometry (e.g. a red bow tie or a headband) — readable from the whole-room camera. Keep the 'rival' role semantics (black ownership bubbles, rival-owned trays) identical. Label stays STRINGS.rivalLabel 'ウェイター'. Optional: a slightly bigger challenger-pose pump for Waiter 2 via the existing challengerPump; skip it if not clean. The entrance label, title, camera close-up, result stage staging (stageAllCharacters), reaction poses (reactionPose.js dejected/celebrate/shrug) and final-question partner must all use Waiter 2 in Round 2. Waiter 1 must be hidden and inert during Round 2.

TUNING (Round 2 only; Round 1 and rematches keep today's values exactly). Add per-level ROUND_TWO configs. Rival (same fields as RIVAL_LEVELS, passed to createRestaurantRival): Normal {speed 4.2 (+17% over 3.6), minSeatedAge 5, share 0.45, hesitationMin 0.4, hesitationMax 0.8, dishNoticeSeconds 0.6}; Challenge {speed 5.15 (+17% over 4.4), minSeatedAge 3, share 0.5, hesitationMin 0.25, hesitationMax 0.6, dishNoticeSeconds 0.45}. Physical movement, interception, no teleport, belt-only dish acquisition and claim rules unchanged — only these parameters differ. Conveyor Round 2 mode (extend CONVEYOR_CONFIG with a roundTwo entry and a startRoundTwo()/startRush(config) path; MIN_DISH_SPACING 1.9 still enforced): Normal {speed 1.26 (+17% over rush 1.08), entryInterval 1.75} ≈ 6.0 visible dishes; Challenge {speed 1.38 (+17% over 1.18), entryInterval 1.4} ≈ 6.8 visible. Patience for Round 2 customers: Normal 28 s, Challenge 25 s (PATIENCE_SECONDS stays 48/38/28 for everything else). Customer pressure: from the first Round 2 second, the director seats customers at its rush pacing with one more simultaneous seated/awaiting customer than the Round 1 rush allowed, capped by the existing table count for the level (do not add tables or change the room layout). If the director has no such knob, add one option (e.g. extraConcurrent) with a unit test. Target language, foods and LESSON strings unchanged.

RESET BETWEEN ROUNDS (one function used by both transitions; tested by repeated rematches): remove all customers (scene objects and arrays: customers, records of the round only if needed for per-round counting — keep cumulative records for stars, see STARS), directorCustomerView, rivalCustomerView, claims (create a new claim registry or clear ownership + reservations + pending claims), dialogue/question state (questionCustomer, questionCommitted, clickQuestionCustomer, listen target, speech cooldown, any open promptAnswer), carried dish (remove mesh), all belt dishes and loose/ready dishes (fresh conveyor instance in the right mode), rival AI instance (fresh createRestaurantRival), rival walk/target/carried dish, conveyor rush state, a fresh serviceDirector for the round, competition score baseline 0–0, resultStage (null) and result label/score-pill classes, rivalChallenge (null or fresh), challenge panel hidden, suppressed keys cleared, focus cancelled, camera back to the gameplay preset/target, notices, combo. Do NOT touch settings, speech/mic-free mode, the player's avatar, or the overlay DOM: DOM elements and event listeners are created once in enter() and reused — a rematch must not add listeners, overlay nodes, lights or characters. No customer from a previous round may remain visible, owned, half-served or counted.

STARS: scoreSession(records) is called at completion. Check what it rates. If it is a ratio (first-try accuracy etc.), keep records cumulative across rounds. If it is count-based, make sure retries cannot lower the stars (e.g. rate the best round). Say which in the summary.

STRINGS (src/config/lesson.js UI.restaurant; add, do not change existing): rivalRematchAsk: 'もう{一回|いっかい} やる？'; rematchChoices: Object.freeze(['もう{一回|いっかい}！', 'おわりにする']); rematchCue: 'もう{一回|いっかい} {勝負|しょうぶ}！'; rival2Title: 'もっと つよい ウェイター！'; rival2Challenge: 'ぼくとも {勝負|しょうぶ}しよう！\nもっと むずかしいよ！'; rival2ChallengeReplies: Object.freeze(['いいよ！{勝負|しょうぶ}だ！', '{負|ま}けないよ！', 'やってみよう！']). Render all of them with the existing furigana renderer.

DEBUG HOOK (read-only, keep every existing field): add progression { round, rivalId, attempt, phase, awaitingChoice, choicesVisible, choices (plain text), roundTotal, roundDone } and rival.config { speed, share, hesitationMin, hesitationMax, dishNoticeSeconds } and conveyor.mode ('solo'|'rush'|'roundTwo') and conveyor speed/entryInterval, customer patienceSeconds per customer, and the character currently acting as rival (rivalCharacter.id or model). rivalChallenge.* must describe the CURRENT encounter (Waiter 2's intro sets it the same way Waiter 1's does). resultStage.* unchanged in meaning; per-round result stage works on each round. Add a counter of challenge-panel listener installs or overlay creations (e.g. hud.overlayCreates) so the controller can confirm rematches do not accumulate them.

TESTS (node --test, deterministic): rivalProgression.test.mjs covers: R1 loss → choice (no round2); R1 draw → choice (identical to loss); chooseRematch → round 1 again with rivalId waiter1, attempt 2, repeated 5x without growth in anything but attempt; chooseFinish → final-question; R1 win → round2-intro, no choice (chooseRematch/chooseFinish return null); startRound2 → round 2 with rivalId waiter2; R2 player/rival/draw → final-question each; after that every call returns null (no round 3). Tuning tests: Round 2 configs are strictly harder than RIVAL_LEVELS[level] (speed higher by 15–20%, hesitation and notice lower, share ≤ 0.5, share not above the Round 1 Challenge share), conveyor Round 2 speed within +15–20% of rush and speed*entryInterval ≥ MIN_DISH_SPACING, Round 2 patience 28/25. Conveyor test: startRoundTwo switches mode and values; director test for the extra-concurrency option. Keep all existing tests passing. The scene wiring is verified by the controller in the browser; make it observable through the debug fields above.
Source-edit hygiene: index.js contains Japanese text, regex literals and template CSS; edit it with the structured edit tool only, never shell/sed/python rewrites.

Rejected alternatives to record: auto-starting a second round on a loss (a loss should end on the child's terms); a rematch prompt between Waiter 1 and Waiter 2 (a win is progress); a shortened Waiter 2 intro (the new opponent must feel like an event); making Waiter 2 hard by giving it most customers (it must win by execution); a Round 3; one absolute Round 2 tuning for both levels (a Normal player would jump past the Challenge rival).
requirements: Round 1 is unchanged: solo deliveries, Waiter 1's cinematic intro and challenge, 0–0, current difficulty, result stage.
Round 1 loss or draw: after the reaction/settle, Waiter 1 asks もう一回 やる？ with exactly two choices in the existing reply UI; Waiter 2 never appears; Talk stays disabled while the choice is shown.

REMATCH: Waiter 1 again at the same RIVAL_LEVELS config, no solo phase, no cinematic, score 0–0, clean room (no stale customers, dishes, claims, carried dish, rival state); repeatable any number of times without accumulating listeners, overlay nodes, characters, customers or score baselines.
FINISH: Waiter 1 asks 'What food do you like?' through the existing final-question path and the minigame completes normally.

Round 1 win: no choice and no final question; Waiter 1 leaves; Waiter 2 (clearly different model, tint, dark apron, accessory; label ウェイター) gets the full existing intro with the Round 2 title, line and replies; any reply starts Round 2 at once.
Round 2: rival active from the first second, no solo trigger, score 0–0, Round 2 rival/conveyor/patience/concurrency tuning active, same target language.
Round 2 result (win, loss or draw) → result stage with Waiter 2 → Waiter 2 asks 'What food do you like?' → completion. No Round 3 path exists.
All debug fields listed in the notes exist and are accurate; all existing debug fields keep working.
DESIGN_DECISIONS.md entry and SPEC.md revised for this pass.
npm test and npm run build pass.
constraints: Do not change Round 1 behaviour, Easy, scoring rules, rival AI rules (only its parameters for Round 2), the result-stage timings, the reveal timings, or any existing lesson string.
No new dependencies and no image/audio asset files; reuse the existing generated jingle.
Keep all existing debug fields working (harness scripts read them); keep competitionOutcome exported from rushTrigger.js and the 'count: 4, total: 9,' literal in index.js.
Do not commit or push; leave changes in the working tree for review.
Edit files with your structured patch/edit tool. If a shell-based edit fails once because of quoting or escaping, switch to the structured mechanism — do not try another escaped variant.
